titulo: ENH: Add DataFrame.headtail() to show first and last N rows together
corpo: ### Feature Type  - [x] Adding new functionality to pandas  - [ ] Changing existing functionality in pandas  - [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas   ### Problem Description  ## Problem Description  When inspecting a large DataFrame, it's common to want a quick look at both the beginning and the end of the data at the same time — for example, to sanity-check that a sort, concat, or time-series load looks correct from start to finish. Currently this requires calling `df.head()` and `df.tail()` separately and manually comparing the two outputs, which is a bit clunky, especially in notebooks where each call produces a separate output block.  ### Feature Description  ## Feature Description  Add a new method, e.g. `DataFrame.headtail(n=5)`, that returns a single DataFrame combining the first `n` and last `n` rows, similar to what `pd.concat([df.head(n), df.tail(n)])` would produce, but as a built-in convenience method. Ideally it would also insert a visual separator (similar to how `describe()` or truncated display uses `...`) to make clear that the middle rows are omitted, rather than implying the rows are contiguous.  Example usage:  ```python df.headtail(5) ```  Possible output:  ```    col1  col2 0     1     a 1     2     b 2     3     c 3     4     d 4     5     e ..  ...   ... 95   96     f 96   97     g 97   98     h 98   99     i 99  100     j ```  ### Alternative Solutions  ## Alternative Solutions  - Users can already do `pd.concat([df.head(n), df.tail(n)])`, but this doesn't include a visual separator and requires an extra import/call pattern. - `pd.set_option('display.max_rows', 10)` combined with printing the full DataFrame gives a similar truncated view, but it changes global display state rather than returning a usable object, and doesn't work well outside of print/repr.  ### Additional Context  ## Additional Context  This would mainly be a display/inspection convenience method, similar in spirit to `head()`/`tail()`/`sample()`, useful for quick EDA on large DataFrames in notebooks and scripts.

titulo: ENH: include cell location in ExcelWriter warning for values exceeding the 32,767 character limit
corpo: ### Feature Type  - [ ] Adding new functionality to pandas  - [x] Changing existing functionality in pandas  - [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas   ### Problem Description  The `ExcelWriter._value_with_fmt` method checks whether a cell value exceeds Excel's 32,767-character limit and currently raises the following warning:  `UserWarning: Cell contents too long (<cell value length>), truncated to 32767 characters`  The current warning message does not identify which cell contains the truncated value. As a result, users need to further inspect the DataFrame separately to determine which value(s) exceeded the limit.  It would be useful for the warning to include the destination cell location. Here is the expected warning message:  `UserWarning: Cell contents too long (<cell value length>) at row <row>, column <column>; truncated to 32767 characters`  That message makes the warning directly actionable and make it easier to identify truncated values during Excel export.  ### Feature Description  Change the  input parameter `val` of the method `ExcelWriter._value_with_fmt` into the **ExcelCell** instance of `cell`. Further update the method to the following format:  ``` def _value_with_fmt(         self, cell: ExcelCell     ) -> tuple[         int | float | bool | str | datetime.datetime | datetime.date, str | None     ]:         """         Convert numpy types to Python types for the Excel writers.          Parameters         ----------         cell : ExcelCell             Spreadsheet cell data that contains the value to be written into cells          Returns         -------         Tuple with the first element being the converted value and the second             being an optional format         """         fmt = None          val = cell.val         if is_integer(val):             val = int(val)         elif is_float(val):             val = float(val)         elif is_bool(val):             val = bool(val)         elif is_decimal(val):             val = Decimal(val)         elif isinstance(val, datetime.datetime):             fmt = self._datetime_format         elif isinstance(val, datetime.date):             fmt = self._date_format         elif isinstance(val, datetime.timedelta):             val = val.total_seconds() / 86400             fmt = "0"         else:             val = str(val)             # GH#56954             # Excel's limitation on cell contents is 32767 characters             # xref https://support.microsoft.com/en-au/office/excel-specifications-and-limits-1672b34d-7043-467e-8e27-269d656771c3             if len(val) > 32767:                 warnings.warn(                     f"Cell contents too long ({len(val)}) in row {cell.row}, column {cell.col};"                     "truncated to 32767 characters",                     UserWarning,                     stacklevel=find_stack_level(),                 )         return val, fmt ```  Update the **four active** function dependency from `cell.val` to only `cell`.  - `def _make_table_cell(...)` on pandas/io/excel/_odswriter.py - `def _write_cells_write_only(...)` on pandas/io/excel/_openpyxl.py - `def _write_cells_normal(...)` on pandas/io/excel/_openpyxl.py - `def _write_cells(...)` on pandas/io/excel/_xlsxwriter.py   ### Alternative Solutions  Users can pre-scan the DataFrame for values exceeding 32,767 characters, but this requires an additional investigation of the data. There is currently no built-in way to obtain the location of the truncated cell from the warning itself.  ### Additional Context  _No response_

titulo: BUG: read_csv with usecols raises IndexError in low-memory mixed-dtype warning path
corpo: ### Pandas version checks  - [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.  - [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.  - [ ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.   ### Reproducible Example  ```python import csv import pandas as pd  file = "repro.csv"  N_COLS = 87 N_ROWS = 20000 TARGET_POS = 50 TARGET_COL = "Overall_Judgment" SWITCH_ROW = 8192  columns = [f"col_{i}" for i in range(N_COLS)] columns[TARGET_POS] = TARGET_COL  with open(file, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:     writer = csv.writer(f)     writer.writerow(columns)      for i in range(N_ROWS):         row = ["x"] * N_COLS          if i < SWITCH_ROW:             row[TARGET_POS] = "YES"         else:             row[TARGET_POS] = ""          writer.writerow(row)  pd.read_csv(file, usecols=[TARGET_COL]) ```  ### Issue Description  On pandas 3.0.5, read_csv raises an internal IndexError when usecols selects a column that is not at position 0 in the original CSV and different low-memory chunks infer different dtypes for that column.  In the reproducible example above, the selected column contains strings in the first low-memory chunk and only missing values in later chunks.  The traceback ends with:      File "pandas/io/parsers/c_parser_wrapper.py", line 361, in _concatenate_chunks         warning_columns.append(column_names[name])                                ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^     IndexError: list index out of range  Changing only TARGET_POS from 50 to 0 makes the IndexError disappear. In that case, read_csv succeeds and emits the expected DtypeWarning instead.  The following workarounds also succeed:  - low_memory=False - explicitly specifying dtype for the selected column - engine="python"  This suggests that the failure occurs in the low-memory mixed-dtype warning path when usecols is used for a column whose original position is greater than 0.  ### Expected Behavior  read_csv should successfully return the selected column.  If different low-memory chunks cause mixed dtype inference, pandas may emit a DtypeWarning, as it does when the selected column is at position 0, but it should not raise an internal IndexError.  ### titulo: pandas `read_pickle` RCE via Ungated `pickle.load` on the Documented Persistence Format
corpo: # pandas `read_pickle` RCE via Ungated `pickle.load` on the Documented Persistence Format  ## Affected Component  - **Package:** `pandas` (pandas-dev); **Module:** `pandas/io/pickle.py` - **Public API:** `pandas.read_pickle(filepath_or_buffer, compression='infer', storage_options=None)` — entry `io/pickle.py:131`, sink at `:233`  ## Affected Versions  - Dynamic verification on pandas 2.2.3 and 2.3.3 (Python 3.10; 3.0.5's wheel requires py≥3.11 — source-verified instead): `io/pickle.py` carries the identical bare `pickle.load` at `:233` (3.0.5). The sink has existed since the API's introduction — ≤3.0.5.  ## Summary  `read_pickle` is the documented counterpart of `pandas.to_pickle` ("pickle it to disk" leads the official user guide's persistence section). The loader is a raw `pickle.load` with no safe-mode parameter, no restriction option, and no environment gate. `compression` selects the codec and `storage_options` selects the fsspec backend — the function unpickles from http/s3 URLs as well, widening the attack surface; neither is a safety switch. Any party who can supply a `.pkl`, `.pkl.gz`, ... (or a URL) that a victim `read_pickle`s executes arbitrary code during deserialization. `TORCH_FORCE_WEIGHTS_ONLY_LOAD` is irrelevant (raw `pickle.load`, not `torch.load`).  ## Vulnerable Code  ```python # pandas/io/pickle.py def read_pickle(     filepath_or_buffer, compression="infer", storage_options=None ):     ...     with get_handle(...) as handles:         ...         return pickle.load(handles.handle)     # :233 (3.0.5)  RCE sink ```  ## Proof of Concept  ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # pandas read_pickle RCE — payload executes during unpickling import os import pandas as pd  class Exploit:     def __reduce__(self):         return (os.system, ('id > /tmp/PWNED_pandas',))  pd.to_pickle(Exploit(), '/tmp/evil_pd.pkl')   # attacker crafts the file  # victim code: the documented reload call; no parameter can block it obj = pd.read_pickle('/tmp/evil_pd.pkl') ```  ## Observed Result  pandas 2.2.3, Python 3.10, Linux: signature `(filepath_or_buffer, compression='infer', storage_options=None)`; the read returned `<class 'int'>` and the call completed cleanly — no exception, no warning.  ## Fix  None. No pandas parameter, environment variable, or config gates this load; the `to_pickle`/`read_pickle` docstring warning about untrusted data is disclosure, not a defense.

titulo: BUG: zoneinfo transition times causes incorrect localization of some Timestamps on 32 bit platforms
corpo: Agent (Claude Opus 5 High)-investigated bug   ```python import pandas as pd  pd.Timestamp("1900-01-01", tz="UTC").tz_convert("US/Eastern") # 32-bit: Timestamp('1899-12-31 19:03:58-0500', tz='US/Eastern')   <-- wrong # 64-bit: Timestamp('1899-12-31 19:00:00-0500', tz='US/Eastern') ```  This is due to how we populate the transition times cache for ZoneInfo objects  ```python import pandas as pd from pandas._libs.tslibs import timezones  # Populate the transition cache for a zoneinfo timezone pd.Timestamp("2000-01-01", tz="US/Eastern")  trans = timezones.dst_cache["zoneinfo/US/Eastern"][0] print(trans[:3]) # [-9223372036854775807                    0 -2717650800000000000] #                                          ^ should be -2**59 * 10**9 ```  which is a result of this line  https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/973d0af19822d4fc8bd58f986e78c533a16dbb53/pandas/_libs/tslibs/timezones.pyx#L398  leads to this failure progression in `test_on_offset_implementations`  > Every TZif file opens with a "big bang" transition at -2**59 seconds, which does not fit in int64 nanoseconds.  > That multiplication wraps it to exactly 0, because 2**59 * 10**9 is congruent to 0 mod 2**64.  > trans[1] therefore becomes 0 (1970) sitting between the NPY_NAT + 1 sentinel and the first real transition, so the array is unsorted — on every platform and for all 597 bundled zones.  > Localizer searches that array with bisect_right_i8, which assumes sorted input, so its answer depends on the array length since every pivot is derived from n.  > Separately, the POSIX-rule validation calls datetime.fromtimestamp(future_ts + 1, timezone.utc), which routes through the platform time_t and raises OverflowError on 32-bit for every future_ts >= 2**31.  > The except handler discards all 124 post-2038 transitions, so len(trans) is 238 on 32-bit versus 362 on 64-bit.  > With 362 the descent probes index 2 (the 1883 EST transition) and returns -18000s; with 238 it lands exactly on the poisoned 0 and returns deltas[0] = -17762s (LMT), off by 3m58s.

titulo: BUG: HDFStore.select with where="cat == None" returns empty DataFrame for Categorical columns instead of matching missing/NaN rows
corpo: ### Pandas version checks  - [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.  - [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/index.html) of pandas.  - [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [main branch](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/getting_started/install.html#installing-the-development-version-of-pandas) of pandas.   ### Reproducible Example  ```python df = pd.DataFrame({"cat": pd.Categorical(["a", np.nan, "b"], categories=["a", "b"])}) df.to_hdf(path, key="df", format="table", data_columns=True)  pd.read_hdf(path, "df", where="cat == None") # returns an empty DataFrame ```  ### Issue Description  When querying an HDF file for empty entries by using `where="cat == None"` or `where="cat == pd.NA"` it returns an empty DataFrame instead of the rows containing the NaNs.   This behavior got introduced in #65793 which aimed to fix a bug returning NaN entries when searching for values that is not one of the categories. It changed `-1` to `-2` as NaN values correspond to `-1`. However, this has the side effect that we cannot search for NaN values anymore as they fall into the same branch.   A possible solution would be to check if the conv_val is a NaN: ``` ...             if conv_val not in metadata:                 # GH#22977 value is not a category; use -2 as a code that                 # matches no row, unlike -1 which is the code for NaN values.                 if pd.isna(conv_val):                     result = -1                 else:                     result = -2 ... ``` (From Line 266 of pandas/core/computation/pytables.py)  I can also open a PR for this issue if this is wanted  ### Expected Behavior  I would expect it to print: ```    cat 1  NaN ```  ### AI Disclosure I used an LLM based approach for research to find this bug and I also used an agentic approach to find a plausible fix. titulo: DOC: user guide SQL section lacks PostgreSQL (psycopg 3) recipes
corpo: ### Pandas version checks  - [x] I have checked that the issue still exists on the latest versions of the docs on `main` [here](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/)   ### Location of the documentation  https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/user_guide/cookbook.html#cookbook-sql  (`doc/source/user_guide/cookbook.rst`, section `cookbook.sql`; the driver notes in `doc/source/user_guide/io.rst` are also psycopg2-only)  ### Documentation problem  The SQL documentation and cookbook examples only reference psycopg2:  - The driver list and the `stream_results` note in the user guide SQL   section mention psycopg2 only. - The dialect string shown for PostgreSQL engines is the generic   `postgresql://` form; `postgresql+psycopg` (psycopg 3) appears nowhere   in the docs. - The cookbook SQL section has no recipes at all — just a link to the   `io.sql` docs and a Stack Overflow answer.  Meanwhile psycopg 3 has been the current major version since 2021 and the recommended driver for new deployments, and the `read_sql` warning for non-SQLAlchemy DBAPI connections ("Other DBAPI2 objects are not tested. Please consider using SQLAlchemy.") sends users to SQLAlchemy without showing the modern dialect string — leading to the common `postgresql+psycopg2` pitfall. Questions about fast bulk loads to PostgreSQL (`to_sql` being slow at scale) also recur on Stack Overflow without a documented cookbook pattern.  ### Suggested fix for documentation  Add a `PostgreSQL (psycopg 3)` subsection at the end of the cookbook SQL section with three small recipes:  1. The recommended connection path: a SQLAlchemy engine on the    `postgresql+psycopg` dialect. 2. A raw-connection pattern (cursor → `DataFrame`, columns from    `cursor.description`), noting the `UserWarning` pandas emits for raw    DBAPI connections. 3. A `COPY`-based bulk-load recipe (staging table + `ON CONFLICT` upsert)    for writes beyond `to_sql`'s performance envelope.  Compared to the current pointer-plus-link, this gives tested, concrete patterns for the most common PostgreSQL integration questions. The recipes come from production usage (an ingestion pipeline loading ~46M daily price rows into PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB) and have been executed as written against PostgreSQL 17 with psycopg 3.3.4 / SQLAlchemy 2.0.52.

titulo: Copilot Chat gets stuck on "Considering..."/"Working..." - "no session host is registered"
corpo: ## Description  GitHub Copilot Chat (VS Code, extension version **0.67.0**, the latest available version) repeatedly gets stuck showing "Considering..." / "Working..." even though no actual processing is happening. This occurs across essentially every new chat session, not tied to a specific project, workspace, or specific tool call.  Once stuck, the chat never recovers no matter how long I wait -- the only way to unblock it is to reload the VS Code window or fully restart VS Code.  ## Evidence found in logs  Looking at `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-*.log`, nearly every recent runtime log file (14 out of 14 checked, spanning roughly the last week) contains this warning, correlated in time with the chat getting stuck:  ``` [WARNING] [rust:copilot_runtime::session::pending_request_flow] pending-request event was not delivered to the session host {"error":"GenericFailure, no session host is registered for session <session-id>"} ```  This suggests the runtime process (`copilot-runtime.exe`) finishes (or attempts to deliver) a response for a given session, but by that point no session host is registered to receive it -- so the response is silently dropped and the chat UI is left showing an in-progress state forever.  ## Steps to reproduce  1. Open VS Code and start a new Copilot Chat session. 2. Send any message / ask any question. 3. Randomly (not always reproducible on demand), the chat gets stuck on "Considering..." / "Working..." indefinitely. 4. Check `%USERPROFILE%\.copilot\logs\process-<pid>.log` around that timestamp -- a `pending-request event was not delivered to the session host` warning appears with `no session host is registered for session <id>`.  ## Workaround found  - Deleting old/stale chat sessions from the session list temporarily resolved the issue, but it recurred later. - Reloading/restarting VS Code always unblocks the current stuck chat (a new runtime process + session host registration presumably resolves the mismatch).  ## Environment  - GitHub Copilot Chat extension version: 0.67.0 (build 1, buildType prod) -- confirmed via `resources\app\extensions\copilot\package.json` in the VS Code install, and confirmed to be the latest available version at the time of reporting. - OS: Windows - Runtime binary: `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` (`copilot-runtime.exe`)  ## Suspected area  Possibly related to recently added multi-window Agent Host support and/or session cleanup features, where a session host can become deregistered (e.g., after a window reload, sleep, or abrupt close) while the runtime still has a pending session id it tries to deliver results to.  ## Request  Please investigate why `pending-request event was not delivered to the session host` occurs and whether the runtime can detect this failure and surface an error/timeout to the chat UI instead of leaving it stuck indefinitely, and/or re-register/recover the session host automatically instead of requiring a full VS Code restart.

The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. --> Switching input sources through GNOME Shell's switcher closes the file rename input in Explorer when VS Code uses its native Wayland backend.  ### Environment  - Ubuntu Linux, GNOME Shell 46.0, Wayland session - VS Code 1.139.1 (`04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`) - Electron 43.6.0, Chromium 150.0.7871.250 - Linux x64 7.0.0-34-generic - English and Russian input sources  Also reproduced in a development build with extensions disabled and a separate user-data directory.  ### Steps to reproduce  1. In a GNOME Wayland session, configure at least two input sources. 2. Launch VS Code with `--ozone-platform=wayland`. 3. Open a folder, select a file in Explorer, and press F2. 4. Edit its name without pressing Enter or Escape. 5. Switch input sources using the configured GNOME shortcut, for example Super+Space.  **Actual:** The rename input closes. A valid pending filename can be accepted even though the user only switched input sources.  **Expected:** The rename input stays open, preserving the pending name and selection so typing can continue.  Launching the same application with `--ozone-platform=x11` avoids the problem. This is a comparison to isolate the Wayland path.  ### Investigation  The blur handler in `FilesRenderer.renderInputBox` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/files/browser/views/explorerViewer.ts`) checks `ownerDocument.hasFocus()` before checking whether the rename input remains the document's active element. Losing page focus can therefore finish editing even when DOM focus has not moved to another element.  A local change that checks `ownerDocument.activeElement` first fixes the input-source switching scenario in manual testing. An Electron regression test using the real renderer reproduces the page-blur case and fails without that change. A second test checks that moving focus to another input still finishes editing.  The automated tests cover page-focus handling; the GNOME input-source switching scenario was verified manually. No Wayland protocol trace was captured.

titulo: Agent host: an automatic rename_chat overwrites a title the user set
corpo: An automatic `rename_chat` replaces a title the user gave an agent-host chat, both in the UI and in the persisted metadata, so the user's title is gone after a reload too.  **Steps to reproduce**  1. Start an agent-host session with an agent that fulfils the host's automatic title reminder (seen with Codex). 2. Rename the session or chat yourself. 3. Send another message. The agent calls `rename_chat` with `automatic: true`. 4. The title changes to the agent's. After a reload, the agent's title is still shown, with `customTitleSource: agent` in the session metadata.  **Expected**  An automatic rename leaves a title the user chose alone. A rename the user explicitly asks the agent for (`automatic` omitted) should still apply.  **Cause**  - `applyRenameChatTool` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/sessionServerTools.ts`) reads `automatic` only to decide whether to run the rename in the background. It does not pass the flag to `ISessionServerToolAccessor.renameChat`. - `AgentService._renameChatFromTool` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`) then persists the agent's title with source `agent` unconditionally. - `SessionTitleContribution` records a user rename with source `user`, but nothing on the tool path checks that source before writing over it.  A fix with tests follows in a PR.  VS Code: `main` at c94d3d7ed24 (agent host) OS: macOS

titulo: Agents: image-preview breadcrumb picker intermittently closes immediately due to delayed webview focus
corpo: <!-- bug_report_template -->  ## Environment  - VS Code: **1.139.0-insider** - Commit: `a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393` - Build date: `2026-09-22T12:05:03+02:00` - OS: Windows (exact Windows build not collected) - Window: **Agents** - Editor: built-in **Image Preview**, displaying an SVG from session artifacts - All extensions disabled: **not tested**; investigation and runtime mitigation were performed without restarting the user's window.  ## Steps to reproduce  1. In the Agents window, open an SVG artifact in the built-in Image Preview editor, with breadcrumbs visible. 2. Click inside the image preview so its webview has focus. 3. Click the final filename breadcrumb to open the sibling-file picker. 4. Repeat if necessary: the failure is timing-dependent.  **Expected:** The breadcrumb picker remains open and focused until the user chooses an item, presses Escape, or deliberately moves focus elsewhere.  **Actual:** The picker appears and immediately disappears. In a captured trace, it was removed approximately **8 ms after its tree gained focus**. This was reproduced on the first automated click, then repeatedly.  Confirmed scope is this Agents/image-preview scenario; other webview editors and the normal workbench have not yet been tested.  ## Investigation: stale asynchronous webview focus steals focus from the picker  Investigated against the live renderer with the global `dbgjs` CLI, using native CDP clicks, focus event tracing, DOM mutation observation, and a non-pausing conditional breakpoint. No restart was required.  The captured runtime call chain was:  ```text BreadcrumbsControl._onSelectEvent   -> editorGroup.focus   -> webviewEditor.focus   -> overlayWebview.focus   -> WebviewElement.focus   -> WebviewElement._doFocus ```  Relevant sources in the affected build:  - [breadcrumbsControl.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/breadcrumbsControl.ts): `_onSelectEvent` unconditionally calls `this._editorGroup.focus()` before opening the picker. The picker hides on `focusTracker.onDidBlur`. - [webviewElement.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/webviewElement.ts): `_doFocus` immediately focuses the outer webview and schedules another focus operation through a 50 ms `ThrottledDelayer`. The delayed callback checks the current active element and calls `_send('focus', undefined)`. - [webview preload](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/a3b0c130bdeeb42c8de4817bd4f5b00b051e8393/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/index.html): the `focus` message handler focuses the inner frame.  The picker loads and focuses its tree asynchronously. The delayed callback can send the webview focus message while the outer iframe is still active, so the existing active-element guard permits it. If the message takes effect after the picker tree gains focus, it takes focus back and the picker closes on blur. If it takes effect before tree focus, the picker survives. A send-time guard does not eliminate this delivery-time race.  Representative failure (relative to the focus-message send):  ```text  0.0 ms  _send('focus'), active element = webview iframe  9.2 ms  breadcrumb tree receives focus 17.6 ms  breadcrumb picker removed ```  ## Controlled runtime experiment  Same live editor and same breadcrumb click, changing only whether the outgoing webview `focus` message was forwarded. Each check occurred 700 ms after clicking. The normal path was tested before and after suppression:  | Condition | Picker dismissed | Picker stayed open | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Normal behavior, before suppression | 2/3 | 1/3 | | Suppress the queued webview focus message | 0/3 | 3/3 | | Normal behavior, restored | 1/3 | 2/3 |  This is a small causal diagnostic, not a randomized statistical study.  A subsequent temporary, reversible hotfix suppressed only outgoing webview `focus` messages while a visible `.monaco-breadcrumbs-picker` existed in the same window. With that guard, **10/10 consecutive clicks kept the picker open and focused**. Separately confirmed that a normal webview focus request without a picker was forwarded and focused the image preview.  The hotfix remains in that renderer until reload, but is **not a proposed production DOM-selector dependency**. All tracing hooks and breakpoints were removed. No source fix has been implemented yet.  ## Proposed fix steps  1. **Avoid focusing the editor pane solely to open the breadcrumb picker.** In `BreadcrumbsControl._onSelectEvent`, separate activating the owning group from transferring DOM focus to its active editor. For the picker-opening path, use the existing group activation API (for example, `this._editorGroup.groupsView.activateGroup(this._editorGroup)`) rather than `this._editorGroup.focus()`, then let the picker take focus. Review the exact placement against both file and outline branches. 2. **Preserve existing reveal/navigation behavior.** Retain editor focusing where the action actually reveals an item, including modifier-click/open-to-side paths. Verify inactive groups become active correctly and picker selection/Escape restore the intended focus. Also test `breadcrumbs.useQuickPick` rather than assuming the same change is safe there. 3. **Consider a general webview hardening follow-up:** invalidate/cancel stale asynchronous focus requests when focus intent changes, rather than relying only on a check before sending the message. Do not disable the picker's blur-to-close behavior or replace the race with a larger arbitrary timeout. 4. **Add a deterministic regression test** that controls the ordering: breadcrumb selection requests editor focus; the delayed webview focus is queued/sent; the picker finishes loading and focuses its tree; the stale request must not steal that focus. Also exercise the opposite ordering, where the picker is ready first. 5. **Validate the full interaction matrix:** repeated SVG/image-preview clicks in Agents; ordinary text-editor breadcrumbs; file and outline pickers; keyboard opening and navigation; selection, Escape and outside-click dismissal; modifier/open-to-side actions; inactive/multiple groups; quick-pick mode; ordinary webview focus with no picker.  The activation-only source change above is a proposed production fix, not yet implemented or validated. The verified live mitigation is the narrowly scoped focus-message guard described above.

`run_in_terminal` returns `Command produced no output` for `git branch --show-current` while chat displays the branch name
corpo: This is a significant bug that affects all the models several times a day: a specific Git tool command is telling the model effectively that Git is in detached `HEAD` mode when it's actually on a branch. This bug has been present for many months. It wastes lots of time and tokens as the model tries to compensate by issuing other Git commands to try to determine whether Git is in detached `HEAD` mode or on a branch.  The bug report below was drafted by Claude Opus 5.5 after discussion.  ## Summary  When Copilot Chat's `run_in_terminal` tool runs `git branch --show-current`, the model receives `Command produced no output`. The chat shows the current branch name as the output of that same tool call. It happens on every attempt in the environment below, and the reporter has seen it repeatedly across sessions and models. `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints the same branch name, and the model receives that output normally.  ## Environment  - VS Code 1.139.1, commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, x64, with GitHub Copilot Chat bundled - OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 - Integrated terminal: Git Bash (Bash 5.3.15, MINGW64, MSYS runtime 3.6.9) - Git: 2.55.0.windows.4 - Model: Claude Opus 5.5. The reporter has seen the same behavior with other models, both more and less capable.  ``` Version: 1.139.1 (user setup) Commit: 04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1 Date: 2026-09-25T03:40:57Z Electron: 43.6.0 ElectronBuildId: 15274685 Chromium: 150.0.7871.250 Node.js: 24.20.0 V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.85.r35379093703.g3514c9a @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.15.35393089353.gfc44743 OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 ```  ## Steps to Reproduce  1. On Windows, set Git Bash as the VS Code integrated terminal shell. Open a Git repository with a named branch checked out, such as `feature/widget`. 2. Ask Copilot Chat to run `git branch --show-current` and to quote the tool result it receives word for word. The model calls `run_in_terminal` with:     ```json    {      "command": "git branch --show-current",      "explanation": "Run the command under investigation and capture the exact result returned to the assistant.",      "goal": "Reproduce missing branch output",      "mode": "sync"    }    ```     `timeout` and `isBackground` are omitted. The other calls listed below also used sync mode; only their `command`, `explanation`, and `goal` values differed. 3. Compare the output the chat shows under the tool call with the result the model quotes.  ## Expected Result  The model receives `feature/widget`, the same output the chat shows. The tool's description says that in sync mode "the full output is returned when the command completes." If the output cannot be captured, the result should say that capture failed, not that the command produced no output.  ## Actual Result  - The chat shows `feature/widget` as the output of the tool call. - The model's tool result contains only this line, after some empty lines:    ```text   Command produced no output   ```  - No exit status is reported. In these calls, a status line appeared only for non-zero exits; see the `git show-ref` row below. - After this command ran as the most recent command in the tool's terminal, the terminal context attached to the next chat request showed that terminal with an empty `Last Command` and `Exit Code: (unknown)`. After `git status --short --branch`, the same context showed that command with `Exit Code: 0`. - When the reporter typed the same command into another integrated Git Bash terminal, it printed `feature/widget` and exited with code 0, according to `terminal_last_command`.  Comparison of `run_in_terminal` results:  | Command | Calls | Result received by the model | |---|---|---| | `git branch --show-current` | 4 | `Command produced no output` | | `git --no-pager branch --show-current` | 1 | `Command produced no output` | | `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` | 1 | `feature/widget` | | `git status --short --branch` | 1 | Complete output, starting with `## feature/widget...origin/feature/widget` | | `git show-ref --quiet --verify <nonexistent ref>` | 2 | `Command produced no output`, then `Command exited with code 1` (correct; this command prints nothing) |  ## Impact  `git branch --show-current` prints nothing when `HEAD` is detached. The false tool result therefore looks like a valid Git result meaning there is no current branch. In the session where this was reproduced, the model said it was checking for a detached `HEAD` and ran another command to find the branch. It then told the user the command had produced no output, which contradicted the output shown in chat. The user cannot see the result the model received, so the problem shows up only when the model says something incorrect. Any agent task that depends on the current branch, such as creating a new branch from it (the task in progress here), starts from a wrong picture of the repository.

CLI agent host supervisor evicts the running Remote-SSH server from the shared server cache; on an NFS home this leaves a broken install (ServerNotExecutable)
corpo:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes (only Remote - SSH is involved, and the bug is in the `code` CLI on the remote) - VS Code Version: 1.136.0 (commit `520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1`, Windows system setup), Remote - SSH 0.128.0, `remote.SSH.useExecServer` at its default `true` - OS Version: client Windows 11 x64; remote Rocky Linux 8.10 (kernel 4.18), `$HOME` on NFSv4.0 Hi! Two colleagues of mine suddenly couldn't connect with Remote-SSH to our Linux build hosts any more, on the same day. Every attempt ended with this, over and over: ``` CodeError(ServerNotExecutable("/home//.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/server/bin/code-server is not executable and permissions could not be restored: No such file or directory (os error 2)")) at Object.resolve (c:\Users\\.vscode\extensions\ms-vscode-remote.remote-ssh-0.128.0\out\extension.js:2:291663) ``` For one of them, moving that `Stable-` folder aside and reconnecting fixed it. We went looking for why it disappeared, and it turns out the CLI's agent host supervisor deletes the editor's server from the shared cache, even while that server is running. On an NFS home the delete only gets halfway, and from then on the CLI reports `ServerNotExecutable` instead of reinstalling. I reproduced the whole chain with the real 1.136.0 CLI; details below. ## What happens All links below are at commit `520fb30b` (1.136.0). I checked that the same code is still on `main` (`90da9001`) today. 1. **Every exec server `serve` starts (or reuses) an agent host supervisor for the user.** `handle_serve` awaits `active_agent_host`, which is `ensure_supervisor_running` ([control_server.rs#L846-L860](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L846-L860), [control_server.rs#L256](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L256), [tunnels.rs#L166](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/tunnels.rs#L166)). There is no condition around it (see also #328397). 2. **The supervisor downloads the latest stable server into the same cache as the editor's server, independent of the client's commit.** At startup it resolves the latest release and calls `ensure_downloaded` ([commands/agent_host.rs#L306-L325](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/agent_host.rs#L306-L325)), and it checks again every 6 hours ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L55](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L55), [#L546-L575](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L546-L575)). It gets `ctx.paths.server_cache` ([commands/agent_host.rs#L288](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/commands/agent_host.rs#L288)), which is `/servers` ([state.rs#L195](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/state.rs#L195)), the same `DownloadCache` the editor's server is installed into ([code_server.rs#L470-L473](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L470-L473)). So a client that is a few releases behind gets one extra server per release. On my own account the supervisor log (`~/.vscode-server/cli/agent-host-stable.log`) shows it downloading 1.136.1, 1.136.2, 1.137.0, 1.138.0, 1.139.0 and 1.139.1 while the client stayed on 1.136.0. 3. **The editor's cache entry is only refreshed when it is first installed.** `DownloadCache::create` returns early without `touch` when the folder already exists ([download_cache.rs#L89-L91](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L89-L91)), and `get_running` does not touch the cache at all ([code_server.rs#L401](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L401)). The editor side uses `server_cache` only through `create` and `delete` (`evict`). The supervisor on the other hand refreshes its own entry through `exists()` ([download_cache.rs#L50-L60](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L50-L60), called at [tunnels/agent_host.rs#L552](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L552)). So the server the user actually works with drifts to the end of `lru.json`, no matter how often they connect. 4. **`touch` keeps 5 entries and deletes the oldest folder without checking whether that server is running** ([download_cache.rs#L119-L139](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/download_cache.rs#L119-L139)). The entry is only dropped from the list if `remove_dir_all` succeeds. For comparison, `prune_stopped_servers` does skip running servers ([paths.rs#L118-L127](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/paths.rs#L118-L127)). 5. **On NFS, deleting a running server fails halfway.** Files the running server still has open turn into `.nfs*` files (here `bin/code-server`, the start script, which the `sh` running it keeps open; it is the only regular file in `bin/`), the directory can't be removed, and `remove_dir_all` stops. What's left is a folder without `bin/code-server` but with `log.txt`, `pid.txt`, `out/`, `node_modules/` and so on, and the entry stays in `lru.json`. 6. **After that the CLI can't recover by itself.** Once the old server process has ended, the next `serve` finds no running server, `create` returns early because the folder exists, and `ensure_executable` gets ENOENT from `std::fs::metadata` ([code_server.rs#L365-L376](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L365-L376)), which is turned into `ServerNotExecutable` ([code_server.rs#L663-L674](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L663-L674)). `handle_serve` only evicts on `ServerUnexpectedExit` ([control_server.rs#L914-L931](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/control_server.rs#L914-L931)), so nothing is cleaned up. Before #316950 (1.122) a missing binary failed at `.spawn()`, which maps to `ServerUnexpectedExit` ([code_server.rs#L676-L680](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs#L676-L680)) and got evicted and reinstalled. 7. **It heals only at the supervisor's next download.** That `touch` tries to delete the same last entry again, and now succeeds because nothing runs from it any more. Until then, which can be days since a supervisor lives for weeks (one of the two users had supervisors running since Aug 17 and Sep 16), every reconnect fails. ## Reproduction Real VS Code 1.136.0 CLI (`https://update.code.visualstudio.com/commit:520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli-linux-x64/stable`), real server builds, in a scratch `--cli-data-dir` on the NFS home. The client side is a small Node script run with VS Code's own Electron (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`): over `ssh` it starts `code command-shell`, does `challenge_issue`/`challenge_verify` with VS Code's bundled `vsda` signer, and sends the `serve` request as defined by `ServeParams` in `protocol.rs`. Supervisor runs use `VSCODE_CLI_INITIAL_AH_VERSION` ([tunnels/agent_host.rs#L66-L71](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1/cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L66-L71)) to replay the releases that came out after 1.136.0; that goes through the same `ensure_downloaded` path the update loop uses. Scripts are at the bottom. **1. A window connects** (serve for `520fb30b`). The CLI downloads and starts 1.136.0; the same `command-shell` also starts a supervisor, which downloads the latest stable (1.139.1): ``` [11:02:07] serverlog: {"line":"Server integrity verified, version: 1.136.0 / 520fb30b2d3d324b4cb2342f6e88e2cd93751de1 / x64 / ","level":0} [11:02:07] serverlog: {"line":"Server started","level":2} [11:02:07] SERVE RESPONSE: success lru.json = ["Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] Stable-04c0d99f…: server Stable-520fb30b…: log.txt pid.txt server ``` **2. One supervisor start per release since then**, window still connected, editor server running: ``` supervisor start pinned to a44adf7f… (1.136.1) lru.json = ["Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 88e44fa0… (1.136.2) lru.json = ["Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 645f29cc… (1.137.0) lru.json = ["Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…","Stable-04c0d99f…"] supervisor start pinned to 7debcd0e… (1.138.0) lru.json = ["Stable-7debcd0e…","Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…"] # (annotation) Stable-04c0d99f…, which nothing ran from, was removed completely here supervisor start pinned to 2242ebbb… (1.139.0) lru.json = ["Stable-2242ebbb…","Stable-7debcd0e…","Stable-645f29cc…","Stable-88e44fa0…","Stable-a44adf7f…","Stable-520fb30b…"] Stable-520fb30b…: log.txt pid.txt server editor server processes: 2 bin/code-server: ls: cannot access '…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server': No such file or directory .nfs files: …/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/.nfs000000000217f4e90000b6c0 ``` **3. Reconnect while the old server still runs**: works, the running server is reused. ``` serverlog: {"line":"Found running server (pid=1121056)","level":2} SERVE RESPONSE: success ``` **4. Reconnect after the old server process has ended** (as after idle shutdown or a reboot), twice: ``` serverlog: {"line":"Checking …/Stable-520fb30b…/log.txt and …/Stable-520fb30b…/pid.txt for a running server...","level":2} serverlog: {"line":"Installing and setting up Visual Studio Code Server...","level":1} serverlog: {"line":"Server setup complete","level":1} serverlog: {"line":"Starting server...","level":2} serverlog: {"line":"Starting server process: \"…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server\"","level":1} SERVE RESPONSE: error {"code":-1,"message":"CodeError(ServerNotExecutable(\"…/Stable-520fb30b…/server/bin/code-server is not executable and permissions could not be restored: No such file or directory (os error 2)\"))"} ``` Same result the second time; `Stable-520fb30b…` (log.txt pid.txt server) and its `lru.json` entry stay as they are. **5. The supervisor restarts** (downloads 1.139.1 again). Now the `touch` removes `Stable-520fb30b…` completely, and the next `serve` reinstalls 1.136.0 and succeeds. **Same thing on a local filesystem** (`/tmp`, xfs, same host): the running 1.136.0 server's folder is removed completely while its processes keep running, and the entry is dropped from `lru.json`. So there the next connection just reinstalls, but the root cause, deleting a server that is in use, is the same, and the still-running server is left without its files (compare the missing-install symptom in #333175). ## What might help Just my reading of the code: - `touch` could skip entries whose server is running, like `prune_stopped_servers` does. - The editor path could refresh its entry on reuse (`create` early return, or `get_running`), so the supervisor's downloads can't push it out. - `ensure_executable` failing with ENOENT could be treated as a broken install and evicted, as before #316950, and `ServerNotExecutable` kept for real permission errors. - The supervisor could keep its downloads apart from the editor's server cache, or not fetch releases the client doesn't use. ## Workaround `"remote.SSH.useExecServer": false` on the client. Remote-SSH then installs to `~/.vscode-server/bin/` without the CLI, no supervisor is started, and the server runs its agent host as its own child process (`--type=agentHost`). Windows that are already open keep exec server mode until they're reloaded. To recover a broken install right away: stop the user's `~/.vscode-server/code-*` processes on the host, move `~/.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-` aside and reconnect. ## Related - Same symptom, no cause yet: #326095, #319809, microsoft/vscode-remote-release#11729 - No way to opt out of the supervisor over SSH: #328397 - Agent host installs disappearing from disk, long-lived stale supervisors: #333175, #334296 - Introduced `ServerNotExecutable` and skips eviction for it: #316950

const h = Buffer.alloc(5); h[0] = 0xdb; h.writeUInt32BE(s.length, 1); return Buffer.concat([h, s]); } if (Array.isArray(value)) { if (value.length >= 16) throw new Error('array too long'); return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x90 | value.length]), ...value.map(encode)]); } const keys = Object.keys(value); if (keys.length >= 16) throw new Error('map too long'); return Buffer.concat([Buffer.from([0x80 | keys.length]), ...keys.flatMap(k => [encode(k), encode(value[k])])]); titulo: Agent Host (Copilot SDK) Windows sandbox: every sandboxed command fails at startup with 0xC0000022 (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED)
corpo: # Agent Host (Copilot SDK) Windows sandbox: every sandboxed command fails at startup with 0xC0000022 (STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED)  ## Environment  | Item | Value | | --- | --- | | VS Code | 1.139.1 (commit `04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1`, x64) | | Copilot runtime | `copilot-runtime.exe` 1.0.85-unstable.r35379093703.g3514c9a | | Copilot SDK package | `@github/copilot-sdk-win32-x64` 1.0.15-unstable.35393089353.gfc44743 | | OS | Windows 11 Enterprise 25H2, build 26200.9448 | | Required update | KB5124008 installed (2026-09-14) | | Session type | Agent Host, Copilot SDK built-in shell (editor window) | | Managed environment | Corporate device (WDAC policies, AppLocker, Microsoft Defender with ASR rules) |  Relevant user settings at the time of the failures:  ```jsonc "chat.editor.preferCopilotHarness": true, "chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "on",   // "off" as a workaround "chat.agent.sandbox.enabledWindows": true,			// "false" as a workaround "chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands": true, "chat.agent.sandbox.allowAutoApprove": true, "chat.agent.sandbox.allowNetwork": true, "chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.windows": {     "allowRead": [],     "allowWrite": ["C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\Temp"],     "denyRead": [] } ```  ## Steps to reproduce  1. On the environment above, enable the SDK sandbox: `"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "on"` and `"chat.agentsandbox.sandbox.enabledWindows": "true"` 2. Start a new Copilot (Agent Host) session in any local folder. 3. Ask the agent to run any command, for example `node --version`, `Get-ChildItem` or `Get-Command node`.  ## Expected  The command runs inside the sandbox and returns its output.  ## Actual  Every sandboxed process fails immediately, in about 1 s, with exit code `-1073741790` (`0xC0000022`, STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED) and **no output at all**:  ``` <shellId: 2 completed with exit code -1073741790> ```  - It affects every executable tried: `powershell.exe` (even a bare `Get-ChildItem`), `node.exe`, and the agent's built-in `grep` tool (`ripgrep exited with code -1073741790`). - The behavior is the same with and without non-ASCII characters in the workspace path (`C:\<dev-with-accent>\...` and `C:\<ascii-path>\...`). - Adding `C:\Program Files\nodejs` to `chat.agent.sandbox.fileSystem.windows` does not help. - `chat.agent.sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands` is `true`, but running the command outside the sandbox is never offered (possibly related: #337310). - With `"chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "off"`, the same commands succeed immediately (`node --version` → `v26.8.2`, exit 0).  The session log marks every failing call as sandboxed:  ``` node --version  | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1302ms Get-Command ... | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1023ms Get-ChildItem   | exit=-1073741790 | sandboxApplied=true | sandboxed=true | 1046ms ```  The Agent Host log contains this error at every session creation, just before the sandbox configuration is applied. It also appears for other sessions:  ``` [error] [Copilot:<session>] Copilot runtime did not report its resolved managed settings; continuing with available sandbox configuration [info]  [Copilot:<session>] Applied SDK sandboxConfig via session.options.update ... [info]  [Copilot:<session>] Managed settings resolved: source=client, managedKeys=permissions, bypassPermissionsDisabled=false, failClosed=false [info]  [Copilot:<session>] Auto-approving sandboxed shell command for tool call <id> ```  ## Diagnostics already performed  - **AppContainer creation works.** For each failing command, `Microsoft-Windows-AppModel-Runtime/Admin` logs `AppContainer Sandbox.{GUID} created successfully` (event 39), then `deleted successfully` (event 41), at the exact timestamp of the command. The failure therefore happens after the container is created, when the process starts or initializes inside it. - **System DLL ACLs are correct.** `icacls C:\Windows\System32\kernel32.dll` grants `(RX)` to `BUILTIN\Users`, `ALL APPLICATION PACKAGES` and `ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES`. - **WDAC / Code Integrity:** no events at the times of the failures. Active corporate policies only block specific apps (Discord, Telegram, Firefox < 149, Python < 3.11). - **AppLocker (EXE and DLL):** no events on the day of the failures. - **Microsoft Defender:** no detection or block related to these processes. The only 1121 events are an unrelated ASR rule (LSASS credential-theft protection, `svchost.exe` → `lsass.exe`), at times that do not match the failures. - **Application / System event logs:** no application errors related to `copilot-runtime`, `powershell`, `node` or `rg` during the failures. - **Windows prerequisite:** KB5124008 is installed, and the build (26200.9448) is newer than the one it ships (26200.9445).  ## Workaround  ```jsonc "chat.agentHost.sdkSandbox.enabledWindows": "off" ```  Then start a new session. Commands then run unsandboxed.  ## Attachments  All files are anonymized: `<user>`, `<machine>`, `<company>`, `<dev>` and `<project>` replace identifying values.  | File | Content | | --- | --- | | `01-environment.txt` | VS Code, Copilot runtime and SDK versions, OS build, KB5124008, ACL of `kernel32.dll` | | `02-settings-sandbox.jsonc` | Sandbox-related user settings | | `03-session-commands.txt` | Every shell/grep call of the affected session, with exit code, `sandboxApplied` and duration (sandbox on, then off) | | `04-agenthost-excerpt.log` | Filtered `agenthost.log` lines (sandbox, runtime, terminal, tool execution, errors), before and after the workaround | | `05-windows-events.txt` | AppModel-Runtime AppContainer events, CodeIntegrity, AppLocker, Defender and Application/System errors during the failures |  ## Suggestions  - Surface the actual failing step when a sandboxed process exits with `0xC0000022` (process creation, DLL load, token or ACL setup), instead of only the exit code. - When `allowUnsandboxedCommands` is `true`, offer "Run outside sandbox" after this kind of startup failure.  ## Related issues (not duplicates)  - github/copilot-cli#4679: Windows sandbox blocks all shell execution, but with an explicit `BaseContainer ... WRITE_DAC` error. - github/copilot-cli#3849: Windows local sandbox fails with `E_NOTIMPL`. - microsoft/vscode#337310: no "run outside sandbox" option despite the bypass setting. [](url)

titulo: Extension host did not start (debugBrk: true) on macOS — js-debug polls ::1 while the extension host listens on 127.0.0.1
corpo: <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ --> Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes  - VS Code Version: 1.139.1 (04c0d99f4fb0d8afe6ce4f0c58e31e183ac3e4b1, arm64) - OS Version: macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)  Steps to Reproduce:  1. On a macOS machine, confirm that `localhost` resolves IPv6-first. This is the macOS default    behavior — the system resolver handles `localhost` itself, so /etc/hosts changes do not affect it:     $ node -e "require('dns').lookup('localhost',{all:true},(e,a)=>console.log(a))"    [ { address: '::1', family: 6 }, { address: '127.0.0.1', family: 4 } ]  2. Open any extension project (reproduced with a plain TypeScript extension project) and press F5    ("Run Extension").  3. The Extension Development Host window opens. After ~10 s VS Code reports:    "Extension host did not start in 10 seconds, it might be stopped on the first line and needs a    debugger to continue. (debugBrk: true)"    and after 60 s: "The local extension host took longer than 60s to send its ready message."  Actual behavior:  The extension host (the debuggee) starts paused at --inspect-brk and listens on IPv4 only:  $ lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN Code Helper (Plugin) <pid> ... TCP 127.0.0.1:53733 (LISTEN)  $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:53733/json/version {"Browser":"node.js/v24.20.0","Protocol-Version":"1.1"}     # host inspector reachable on IPv4  But the built-in JavaScript debugger (ms-vscode.js-debug 1.117.0) polls ::1:<port> and never falls back to 127.0.0.1. The Debug Console repeats the following ~91 times within the 10 s window:  RequestError: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:53733     at ClientRequest.<anonymous> (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js:23:14613)  Since the debugger can never attach, the extension host stays paused forever.  Local verification that this is an address-family mismatch, not a missing listener (same machine):  $ node -e "require('http').get({host:'localhost',port:53733,path:'/json/version',autoSelectFamily:false},r=>{...}).on('error',e=>console.log('ERR:',e.message))" ERR: connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:53733        # identical to the js-debug error $ node --dns-result-order=ipv4first -e "<same request>" OK 200 $ curl -s http://localhost:53733/json/version OK  Expected behavior:  js-debug's attach/polling of the extension-host inspector should fall back across address families (as curl and Node's default behavior do), or both sides should agree on the loopback address.  Attempted workarounds — none changed the behavior:  - Launching VS Code as: code --dns-result-order=ipv4first - Commenting out "::1 localhost" in /etc/hosts and fully restarting VS Code. Note that on macOS this   has no effect on resolving `localhost` (the system resolver keeps returning ::1 first, as shown above).  Notes:  - The same symptom was reported in the closed #140536 (2022). Based on the Debug Console output, the   extension-host attach path still only attempts ::1 — no fallback to 127.0.0.1 is attempted (the   listener is verifiably reachable on 127.0.0.1 during the whole failure window). - Reading the shipped (minified) sources: VS Code starts the debuggee host with   --inspect-brk=127.0.0.1:<port> (workbench.desktop.main.js, localProcessExtensionHost), while   js-debug's extension-host launch polls http://localhost:<port>   (ms-vscode.js-debug/src/extension.js), with no address-family fallback on that path. - Happy to provide full Debug Console logs or run further diagnostics. If this belongs in   vscode-js-debug, please feel free to transfer.  [0926-after-F5.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32681019/0926-after-F5.log)

titulo: [chat-perf] TTFT/layoutDurationMs regressed 29–45% in large-codeblock, long-prose, file-links, thinking-response scenarios
corpo: ### Summary *New regression detected*: Significant increases in `timeToFirstToken` (+29–45%) and `layoutDurationMs` (+21%) in the following chat scenarios: **large-codeblock, long-prose, file-links, thinking-response**. These are well outside the baseline window's normal noise and represent a clear step up from previous runs.  ### Evidence - **large-codeblock**: TTFT 507ms (was 373ms ±18), layoutDurationMs 207ms (was 171ms ±2.8) - **long-prose**: TTFT 494ms (was 384ms ±13) - **file-links**: TTFT 552ms (was 382ms ±5.6) - **thinking-response**: TTFT 535ms (was 397ms ±17)  All are >100ms above the baseline mean and well outside baseline spread.  **Trend:** - All four metrics show a sharp increase in the current run, after a long period of stability (see baseline window: no similar spikes, no prior regressions). - The regression is not present in the last 6 baseline runs, all of which were stable.  **Suspect Commits:** - The regression likely landed between the last baseline and this run. The most suspicious are recent changes touching chat/session/layout logic:   - 4ccdb71 (sandy081): "sessions: Synchronize live last turn changes" — touches chat/session logic, landed just before this regression.   - 1e3ed44 (sandy081): "agentHost: Scope server tools to exact chats" — also landed in this window, touches chat/agent logic.  ### Suggested Action - Bisect between the last good baseline and this run, focusing on 4ccdb71 and 1e3ed44 as likely culprits. - Review changes in chat/session/layout code for performance impact on TTFT/layout. - Roll back or optimize as needed.  --- **Please triage promptly: these are major regressions in core chat responsiveness.**

titulo: Archiving a chat deletes a worktree still used by another chat
corpo: <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->  - A session created a worktree, and a second chat opened in the editor used the same worktree to create PR #338066. - Archiving the original chat from the Agents window consistently deletes the worktree. - The second chat remains visible but becomes unusable.  ### Steps to reproduce  1. Start a session that creates and uses a worktree. 2. Within that session, create another chat in the editor window. 3. Use the second chat to create a pull request from the worktree. 4. Archive the original chat in the Agents window. 5. Open the remaining chat.  - **Expected:** Archiving one chat does not delete a worktree still referenced by another non-archived chat, especially one associated with an active PR. Alternatively, if archival applies to the entire owning session, all dependent chats should be archived together with a clear warning. - **Actual:** The worktree is deleted every time, but the dependent chat remains and fails to load with `SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError`. - **Extensions disabled:** Not checked. - **Reproduction:** Every time.  ![A remaining chat showing PR 338066 and SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError after its worktree path was deleted and redacted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64932440-db80-4584-bc15-01c15d4ae13b)  <details> <summary>Details for investigation</summary>  The remaining chat reports:  ```text Error: (workingDirectoryFailed) SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError: This session couldn't be loaded because its working directory no longer exists: <deleted worktree path> ```  Related but distinct: #337325 concerns already-deleted worktrees remaining selectable.  </details>

titulo: Copilot Agent Window: BYOK custom models register in Chat but fail in agent sessions (session.model.switchTo 'not registered')
corpo:
### Summary
 
 BYOK custom models (`customendpoint/<vendor>/<model>` — e.g. Ollama Cloud endpoints configured through the supported BYOK path: `chatLanguageModels.json` + `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`) work fine in **Chat**, but cannot be selected in **Agent Window / agent host sessions**:
 
 ```
 Error: (modelSelectionFailed) Error: Request session.model.switchTo failed with message:
 Provider model 'customendpoint/Ollama Cloud/glm-5.3-flash:cloud' is not registered
 ```
 
 The agent host's session registry contains only built-in models. The BYOK models are wired to the loopback proxy at boot, but never reach the session SDK registry that `session.model.switchTo` consults.
 
 ### What works / what doesn't
 
 In Chat: BYOK models are listed and selectable. ✓
 
 In the Agent Window (agent host session):
 
 ```
 [Copilot:boot] Wired 52 BYOK model(s) across 3 provider(s) via loopback proxy http://127.0.0.1:56113
 ...
 [Copilot:c7f7565c] Changing model to: customendpoint/Ollama Cloud/glm-5.3-flash:cloud
 [Copilot] Found 31 models: Auto, Claude Sonnet 5, ...   <-- registry unchanged, zero customendpoint entries
 [AgentSideEffects] modelSelection failed ... Provider model 'customendpoint/...' is not registered
 ```
 
 The host resolves a BYOK session config for boot (`_resolveByokSessionConfig(boot)` in the session launcher code, `copilotSessionLauncher`) containing all the models — but nothing plumbs them into the session registry at boot, and the `BYOK bridge changed` handler (`_refreshByokModels`) only refreshes the wire-side catalog.
 
 ### Two runtime semantics we discovered empirically
 
 While investigating we instrumented the runtime and found two behaviors that (if confirmed) would be worth documenting upstream, since they fundamentally constrain how a host can register BYOK models into an agent session:
 
 **1. `session.rpc.provider.add` accepts exactly one referencing per provider name.**
 
 Any call after the first — even with `providers: []` — is rejected wholesale with:
 
 ```
 Error: Request session.provider.add failed with message: Duplicate BYOK provider name customendpoint.
 ```
 
 ...without registering the payload models. A successful registration is necessarily a **single batch call**:
 
 ```ts
 session.rpc.provider.add({ sessionId, providers: <all BYOK providers>, models: <all BYOK models> });
 ```
 
 Verified empirically: per-model registration attempts produced 520 rejected calls in a single boot session; one single batch call returned success and all models became switch-selectable.
 
 **2. Permission mode `allow-all` is rejected by the SDK policy in headless agent sessions.**
 
 `_getSdkPermissionMode()` maps an auto-approve session (`autoApprove` level) to `allow-all`, then the first send fails with:
 
 ```
 [Copilot] Syncing permission mode: source=turn-start, agentMode=interactive, configuredLevel=autoApprove, sdkMode=allow-all, ...
 error: Copilot SDK rejected permission mode 'allow-all'  ->  sendFailed
 ```
 
 A graceful fallback (e.g. `assisted`) — or a documented way to enable the mode for agent hosts — would remove the trap.
 
 ### Repro
 
 1. Configure a BYOK custom endpoint (any vendor) via the supported BYOK settings; verify it works in Chat.
 2. Open the Agent Window; in an agent session, switch the model to the BYOK model.
 3. Observe `modelSelectionFailed ... not registered` in the agent host log, with the session registry logging built-ins only.
 
 ### Proposal / ask
 
 - At agent session boot (or on `BYOK bridge changed`), register the resolved BYOK models into the session SDK registry — presumably as a single batch `provider.add` per provider (see semantic 1) in the boot path of `copilotSessionLauncher` / `_buildSessionConfig`.
 - Document the `provider.add` single-reference semantics (e.g. in `@github/copilot-sdk` types) and the permission-mode policy expectations for agent hosts.
 
 ### Environment
 
 - VS Code 1.139.0 (user setup), commit `04c0d99f4f`, Windows 11 x64
 - Agent host: `resources/app/out/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostMain.js`
 - Copilot runtime: `@github/copilot-win32-x64` (SDK surface: `@github/copilot-sdk` public types)
 
 Thanks! Happy to provide full boot logs if useful.

titulo: Remote agent sessions do not discover host MCP servers until messaged locally
corpo: ## Type of Issue  Bug  ## Reproduction  Both the local laptop and remote dev box have the Notion MCP server configured.  1. From the laptop, start an agent session on the dev box. 2. From the laptop, ask the remote session whether it has the Notion MCP server. 3. Observe that the session reports that it does not. 4. On the dev box, message the same session directly and ask the same question. 5. Observe that the session now reports that the Notion MCP server is available. 6. From the laptop, ask the same session again. 7. Observe that it now reports the server as available there as well.  ## Expected Behavior  A remote session should discover MCP servers configured on the host machine when it starts, regardless of whether the session has first been messaged locally on that host.  ## Actual Behavior  Host MCP servers are unavailable to a remotely initiated session until the same session is messaged locally on the host machine. After that local interaction, the MCP server becomes available remotely too.  ## Additional Context  Agent Host logs were captured as `ah-logs-Notion-access-inquiry.zip` in the original report.

titulo: Let primary AI agents delegate routine work to local models
corpo: <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ --> <!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ --> <!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->  <!-- Describe the feature you'd like. --> VS Code already supports agent workflows, subagents, and local/BYOK models. I’d like those pieces connected more intelligently. The idea is simple: let a high-capability reasoning model handle the larger task—architecture, difficult debugging, integration and review—while automatically delegating bounded, routine work to a local coding model such as Qwen Coder. For example: Primary reasoning model → local Qwen Coder → tests/results → primary model review The local model could handle repository searches, repetitive edits, simple refactors, documentation, test generation and other low-risk work. The primary model would remain responsible for the overall task and review everything returned by the local agent. This would reduce premium-model usage and latency, improve privacy, make useful use of local hardware, and reserve the strongest model for the work that actually needs it. In short: don’t make one expensive model do everything. Let the coordinator intelligently distribute the work among available models. There are already related issues around BYOK models being used as subagents (#333802 and #331904), so much of the underlying infrastructure appears to exist. What I’m asking for is the orchestration layer that makes heterogeneous models work together as one coding system.

titulo: Add guard clause for API key validation in AzureOpenAIEndpoint
corpo: While reviewing the `AzureOpenAIEndpoint` class, I noticed that header generation proceeds without validating whether the API key or Entra ID token (`this._apiKey`) is actually present.  To improve defensive programming and fail early with a clear error when credentials are missing, I'd like to introduce a guard clause at the beginning of the `getExtraHeaders()` method.  ### Proposed Changes: - Add a check for `this._apiKey` in `getExtraHeaders()` to throw an explicit error if missing.

titulo: Managed enabledPlugins refresh does not reconcile active Agent Host sessions
corpo: ## Problem  VS Code does not have an explicit host-side convergence path for managed `enabledPlugins` changes that arrive after an Agent Host session has started.  The runtime refreshes managed settings for long-running sessions, but a refreshed policy can be present while the active session retains its previous plugin inventory and plugin-provided skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and extensions. Users may need a new session or application restart before a managed plugin appears or disappears.  A September 24 enterprise customer meeting provided a concrete example: a managed marketplace appeared after refresh/restart, while the plugin did not become enabled for roughly 24 hours. The customer expected every new session or surface restart to fetch current settings, and already-running clients to apply hourly updates without requiring a restart.  ## Expected behavior  - VS Code responds to each applied managed-settings generation. - Managed plugin installation, enablement, disablement, and contributed resources converge in the active session when safe. - If a new session or subsystem reload is required, the product states that explicitly and offers a recovery path instead of silently retaining stale behavior. - Policy withdrawal removes contributions on the same documented lifecycle. - Tests cover adding and withdrawing `enabledPlugins` while an Agent Host session remains open.  ## Related work  - github/copilot-agent-runtime#22922 tracks the host-independent runtime contract. - github/github-app#16986 tracks the Copilot App integration. - microsoft/vscode#338071 fixed force-enablement for an already-installed plugin, but not live refresh convergence.

titulo: Webview can stay on its old content when its HTML is replaced while that content is still loading
corpo: - VS Code version: 1.139.1 (latest stable) and `main` (949b097). The webview host page is byte-identical in both. - OS: any. The logic is platform-independent; I reproduced it in Chromium on Windows 11.  ## What happens  If a webview's HTML is replaced while the previous content is still loading, the new content can get stuck in `pending-frame` forever:  - The old content stays on screen. - Every `postMessage` to the webview is queued for the new frame and never delivered. - Messages from the new content to the host still arrive, so to the embedder the webview looks alive but deaf.  ## Why  The host page shows new content in a pending frame, which becomes the active frame when it loads, or after a 200ms fallback timer when its load is slow. While a pending frame exists, every message to the webview is queued for it (L1246-L1254).  The fallback timer lives in one variable, `loadTimeout` (L420), shared by every frame. Each frame's `load` listener clears whatever timer that variable holds at the time:  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/949b097abf4e9b62d9153e885657b32e01115920/src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/index.html#L1153-L1172  The failing sequence:  1. Content A is set. Its load is slow, so its fallback makes it the active frame while its own `load` event is still pending. 2. Content B is set. `hookupOnLoadHandlers` puts B's fallback timer into `loadTimeout`. 3. A's `load` event fires within B's 200ms window. A's listener clears B's timer, then calls `onLoad` for A, which does nothing because A is no longer the pending frame. 4. B's own `load` event later finds `loadTimeout` empty and does nothing.  B is never activated, and nothing retries.  It needs A's load to finish after B has been written. So it shows up when content with slow-loading parts, such as large inline scripts or nested frames, is replaced in quick succession, and much more often on slow or software-rendered machines.  ## Steps to reproduce  This drives the real `index.html` from an embedding page, the way a webview element does:  1. Load the host page from its `<parentOriginHash>` host, for example `<hash>.localhost`, with `disableServiceWorker`. 2. Send `content` A, whose body holds its own load until told otherwise:    ```html    <iframe id="hold"></iframe>    <script>const held = document.getElementById('hold').contentDocument; held.open(); held.write('held');</script>    ``` 3. Wait until A is `active-frame`. The fallback does this after about 200ms. 4. Send `content` B, which holds its load the same way. 5. As soon as B appears in `pending-frame`, close A's held document (`held.close()`), which fires A's `load`. 6. Release B's hold, then post a message to the webview.  **Expected:** B becomes the active frame and receives the message.  **Actual:** B stays pending, A stays on screen, and the message never arrives.  In 5 runs of each, with `main`'s `index.html` served from its hash host in Chromium:  | Scenario | Stock `index.html` | With a per-frame timer | |---|---|---| | Race above | 0 of 5 recover | 5 of 5 recover | | Control: A finishes loading before B is sent | 5 of 5 fine | 5 of 5 fine |  A fix that gives each frame its own timer follows as a PR.

titulo: Refactor css variable validator to use a strongly-typed schema for known variables
corpo: While reviewing the CSS variable validation logic, I noticed that the parsed JSON content from `vscode-known-variables.json` is currently untyped (`any`-like).   To improve type safety and adhere strictly to TypeScript best practices within the codebase, I'd like to introduce a dedicated interface (`IKnownVariablesSchema`) for the parsed JSON structure.  ### Proposed Changes: - Add an `IKnownVariablesSchema` interface defining `colors`, `others`, and optional `sizes`. - Type cast the `JSON.parse` result explicitly to ensure type safety.

titulo: Managed enabledPlugins true does not force-enable an installed plugin
corpo: ## Problem  When the enterprise `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy maps an installed `plugin@marketplace` identity to `true`, the plugin is still governed by the stored user or workspace enablement choice. A user can disable it, removing its contributed hooks, skills, tools, or other customizations even though organization policy requires it.  The inverse policy value already behaves differently: a plugin mapped to `false` is disabled and cannot be re-enabled.  ## Expected behavior  For plugins that are already installed and discovered:  - Managed `true` force-enables the exact `plugin@marketplace` identity. - Managed `false` force-disables it. - Local profile and workspace enablement writes cannot override either managed value. - The underlying user choice is preserved and becomes effective again if the managed entry is removed. - Plugins omitted from policy remain user-controlled; the setting stays additive rather than becoming an allowlist. - A force-enabled plugin cannot be disabled or uninstalled through the plugin management UI.  ## Verification  Configure three installed fixture plugins:  ```json {   "enabledPlugins": {     "required-demo@example-marketplace": true,     "blocked-demo@example-marketplace": false   } } ```  Leave a third plugin omitted from policy, and pre-seed `required-demo` as locally disabled.  Verify that:  1. `required-demo` is enabled and its switch is locked. 2. `blocked-demo` is disabled and its switch is locked. 3. The omitted plugin remains user-toggleable. 4. The required plugin has no uninstall action. 5. Removing the policy entries restores the stored local choices. 6. A same-named plugin from another marketplace does not inherit the managed decision.  Fixed by #337209.  ## Scope  This issue covers enablement and management controls for plugins that are already installed and discovered. Installation or restoration of a missing required plugin is tracked separately in #337221. Failure behavior when a required plugin cannot be acquired is also outside this issue.
